item.title: California school systems face red ink despite boosts in education spending
item.description: While the state borrows $5.6 billion from education, districts throughout the state are struggling to balance their own budgets this year.

item.title: 5 things we learned by spending time in Los Angeles senior centers
item.description: No two California senior centers are alike. They're shaped by their neighborhoods with programs that range from gym classes to meals, movie nights and more.

item.title: ‘We wanted to find new friends’: See how older Californians are proving that senior isolation isn’t inevitable
item.description: Los Angeles senior centers are rebounding from COVID shutdowns and offering new programs for older adults. See how life changed for participants since the pandemic.

item.title: California can sidestep scandal and banish bias while counting votes
item.description: Open source voting systems are more transparent and cheaper than the state’s current contract with Smartmatic, which is facing bribery charges.

item.title: How an aging California is turning to senior centers for romance, community and health
item.description: No two senior centers are alike. We visited three very different venues in L.A. to learn how they're changing to meet the needs of California's aging population.

item.title: CA senior centers offer critical services
item.description: By 2030, the number of Californians age 65 and older will likely exceed those who are under 18. Some of these estimated 8.6 million residents will experience loss and grief, intensifying feelings of loneliness. But as CalMatters’ Joe Garcia explains, senior centers can offer a vital respite — helping elders live out their golden years […]

item.description: No hay dos centros para personas mayores iguales. Se adaptan a sus vecindarios y ofrecen programas que abarcan desde clases de gimnasia hasta comidas, noches de cine y más.

item.description: No hay dos centros para personas mayores iguales. Visitamos tres centros muy diferentes en Los Ángeles para conocer cómo están cambiando para satisfacer las necesidades de la población de la tercera edad de California.

item.title: San Diego teachers cancel strike as deadline neared; district to address demands over special education
item.description: San Diego teachers canceled their planned Feb. 26 strike after reaching a tentative agreement with the San Diego Unified School District to increase special education staffing, provide additional teacher support and stipends, and secure future pay raises pending restoration of state funding.

item.title: “Queríamos encontrar nuevos amigos”: Las personas mayores de California demuestran que el aislamiento no es inevitable
item.description: Los centros para personas mayores de Los Ángeles se están recuperando de los cierres por la COVID-19 y ofrecen nuevos programas para adultos mayores. Vea cómo cambió la vida de los participantes desde la pandemia.
